newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile inflation creeps up to 0.8 pct in February.
newsitem.headline: Chile inflation creeps up to 0.8 pct in February.

text.p: Consumer prices rose 0.8 percent in Chile last month, led by sharply higher food prices, and bringing inflation over the past year to 7.2 percent, the government said.
The rate was up markedly from 0.5 percent in February 1996 and 0.5 percent in January, said the National Statistics Institute's monthly report.
Food prices climbed 1.5 percent, a brisk rise in line with expectations because severe drought in central Chile has cut into farm production.
Housing prices rose 0.7 percent, followed by transport and communications at 0.6 percent, and the catch-all other category at 0.6 percent. Clothing prices fell 1.3 percent.

The February rise brought inflation to 1.3 percent in the first two months of the year and 7.2 percent over the past 12 months, said the institute. Prices rose 7.8 percent in the 12 months to February 1996.
The government's target is to bring consumer inflation under six percent this year after it ended 1996 at 6.6 percent.
